cards.front: What does { [K in keyof T]: ... } mean?
cards.meaning: A mapped type builds a new object type by iterating keys. For each key K in keyof T, emit a property with that name and a computed value type — often T[K] or a transform. You can change value types, add or remove ? / readonly, or rename keys with as.

cards.front: Are Partial, Required, Readonly, Pick, and Record magic builtins?
cards.meaning: No. They are implemented as mapped types, not compiler magic. Thinking Partial or Readonly are special primitives is a listed misconception.

cards.front: What does Flags<T> = { [K in keyof T]: boolean } produce?
cards.meaning: Same keys as T but every value type becomes boolean — a typical feature-flag shape over an interface.
cards.example: type FeatureFlags = Flags<FeatureSet>; // { darkMode: boolean; betaAccess: boolean }

cards.front: What is the mental model, and what is an identity map?
cards.meaning: For each key K in keyof T, emit property K with a computed type, often T[K] or a transform of it. type Mirror<T> = { [K in keyof T]: T[K] } is the identity map — same keys and same value types.
cards.example: type Mirror<T> = { [K in keyof T]: T[K] };

cards.front: Why do mapped types exist?
cards.meaning: Object shapes repeat with systematic changes: same keys all optional, same keys readonly, getters for each field. Mapped types express that once instead of re-listing fields.

cards.front: Do mapped types loop at runtime?
cards.meaning: No. They are erased — no runtime loop; only a compile-time type. Like other TypeScript type machinery, they do not produce JS iteration.

cards.front: How do you implement Partial<T>?
cards.meaning: type MyPartial<T> = { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] }; — adds optional ? to every property. Built-in Partial is this mapped type, not magic.
cards.example: type MyPartial<T> = { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] };

cards.front: How do you implement Readonly<T> as a mapped type?
cards.meaning: type MyReadonly<T> = { readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] }; — re-declares each key with readonly and the same value type.
cards.example: type MyReadonly<T> = { readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] };

cards.front: What does [K in keyof T]-? do?
cards.meaning: The -? modifier removes optionality from each key — how Required is implemented. type MyRequired<T> = { [K in keyof T]-?: T[K] }.
cards.example: type MyRequired<T> = { [K in keyof T]-?: T[K] };

cards.front: How do you strip readonly with a mapped type?
cards.meaning: type MyMutable<T> = { -readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] };. The - prefix removes the readonly modifier the way -? removes optionality.

cards.front: What are +? and +readonly for?
cards.meaning: They exist for symmetry with the minus forms. Usually you write ? / readonly without the +; Partial adds ? and Readonly adds readonly that way.

cards.front: Does MyReadonly<T> equal Object.freeze?
cards.meaning: No. readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] makes each property readonly at compile time — obj.prop = x errors through that type. It does not Object.freeze at runtime. Use freeze or immutable libraries if you need runtime immutability. Nested objects are not recursively readonly unless you write a deep mapped type.

cards.front: How is Pick implemented, and what does it map over?
cards.meaning: type MyPick<T, K extends keyof T> = { [P in K]: T[P] }. Pick maps over a subset of keys K, not necessarily all of keyof T. Forgetting K extends keyof T on Pick-like helpers is a listed trap.
cards.example: type MyPick<T, K extends keyof T> = { [P in K]: T[P] };

cards.front: How is Record implemented?
cards.meaning: type MyRecord<K extends string | number | symbol, V> = { [P in K]: V }. Record maps over an arbitrary key union K with uniform value type V — dictionaries and exhaustive key maps.
cards.example: type MyRecord<K extends string | number | symbol, V> = { [P in K]: V };

cards.front: How does Omit relate to mapped and conditional types?
cards.meaning: Omit is typically Pick plus Exclude on keys — not a separate primitive. type MyOmit<T, K extends keyof any> = Pick<T, Exclude<keyof T, K>>.
cards.example: type MyOmit<T, K extends keyof any> = Pick<T, Exclude<keyof T, K>>;

cards.front: What does K in keyof T as `get${Capitalize<...>}` produce?
cards.meaning: Key remapping with as renames emitted keys. Getters<Person> becomes { getName: () => string; getAge: () => number }. After in, as NewKey renames (or filters) the emitted key; template literals build names like on${Capitalize<…>}.
cards.example: [K in keyof T as `get${Capitalize<string & K>}`]: () => T[K]

cards.front: What does as NewKey do after in in a mapped type?
cards.meaning: It renames or filters the emitted key. Template literals build new names; mapping a key to never drops it. This is TS 4.1+ key remapping.

cards.front: How do you drop keys with as never?
cards.meaning: Map the key to never with as to omit it. PublicOnly uses K extends `_${string}` ? never : K to exclude _prefixed fields. The same idea strips function keys.
cards.example: [K in keyof T as K extends `_${string}` ? never : K]: T[K]

cards.front: Why write string & K in a template remapping?
cards.meaning: keyof can include symbol and number, while template literal types expect string. string & K (or Exclude<K, symbol> patterns) narrows so Capitalize and templates type-check. Forgetting symbol keys is a listed trap.

cards.front: How does NonFunctionPropertyNames filter keys via an indexed map?
cards.meaning: Map each K to never or K depending on whether T[K] extends Function, then index with [keyof T] to get the remaining key union. NonFunctionProps is Pick<T, NonFunctionPropertyNames<T>>.
cards.example: { [K in keyof T]: T[K] extends Function ? never : K }[keyof T]

cards.front: How do you filter function keys with as in a mapped type?
cards.meaning: type NonFunctionProps2<T> = { [K in keyof T as T[K] extends Function ? never : K]: T[K] }. Pattern: filter keys with conditionals, map values with T[K] transforms.

cards.front: What is the split between filtering keys and mapping values?
cards.meaning: Filter keys with conditionals (as never, or a key union plus Pick). Map values with T[K] transforms. Combining mapped and conditional types is that two-step pattern.

cards.front: Are Partial and Readonly deep?
cards.meaning: No — they are shallow. Nested objects are not recursively optional or readonly unless you write a deep mapped type. Expecting deep immutability or optionality from shallow maps is a listed mistake.

cards.front: What is the DeepPartial sketch, and what should you skip in interviews?
cards.meaning: type DeepPartial<T> = { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] extends object ? DeepPartial<T[K]> : T[K] }. Arrays, Date, and functions are edge cases — keep the sketch simple in interviews unless asked. Overbuilding deep recursive maps for a one-off DTO is a listed mistake.
cards.example: [K in keyof T]?: T[K] extends object ? DeepPartial<T[K]> : T[K]

cards.front: What is a homomorphic mapped type, at awareness level?
cards.meaning: When you write { [K in keyof T]: … } over keyof T, TypeScript often preserves optional and readonly modifiers from T in subtle homomorphic ways unless you override with +/-. You do not need the full theory — know that modifiers on the map are how you force optional, required, or readonly.

cards.front: Why does Partial add ? explicitly instead of relying on homomorphism?
cards.meaning: Homomorphic maps can preserve T's modifiers unless you override. Partial forces ? on every key; Required uses -? to strip optionality. That is why the modifiers are written explicitly.

cards.front: Does the readonly mapped modifier freeze at runtime?
cards.meaning: No. Believing readonly freezes at runtime is a listed misconception. It is compile-time only; use Object.freeze or an immutable library for runtime.

cards.front: What constraint must K have on a Pick-like helper?
cards.meaning: K extends keyof T. Without it, you can map keys that do not exist on T. The constraint is part of the homemade Pick signature.

cards.front: How do keyof T and T[K] connect to mapped types?
cards.meaning: keyof T plus T[K] is the iteration: map over property names and look up each value type. That is how Partial, Readonly, Pick, and Record are built. The utility-types unit consumes this machinery.

cards.front: What do +/- ? and readonly do on a mapped type?
cards.meaning: They force modifiers: add or remove optionality and readonly, overriding homomorphic preservation from T.

cards.front: What does as NewKey | never connect to?
cards.meaning: Rename keys with a new name, or filter them by mapping to never. Template remapping and PublicOnly both sit on that fork.

cards.front: How do T[K] extends … ? checks show up inside maps?
cards.meaning: As conditional filters on keys or branches on value types — advanced derivations like non-function props and DeepPartial. Mapped types next combine with the conditional-types unit.

cards.front: What mapped-type sketch should you be able to write first?
cards.meaning: { [K in keyof T]: T[K] } — iterate keys, keep value types. Then implement Readonly, Partial, and Required with modifiers; contrast compile-time readonly with Object.freeze; show a simple as remapping; sketch Omit as Exclude plus Pick.
